title: City Rush: Checkpoint Rally
description: A miniature toy car races through a virtual city collecting glowing checkpoints scattered across the streets. The player steers the car using arrow keys, must hit all checkpoints in order within a time limit, and can honk the horn to reveal the next checkpoint's direction. A HUD tracks progress, elapsed time, and remaining checkpoints.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap/CDN) that implements a checkpoint rally game combining VirtualCity.glb and ToyCar.glb. Load VirtualCity.glb as the environment placed at the origin. Load ToyCar.glb scaled to fit proportionally as a small car navigating the city streets. Camera: use a third-person chase camera that smoothly follows behind and above the car using lerp-based interpolation. Lighting: add a warm DirectionalLight with shadows enabled, a soft AmbientLight, and a subtle blue HemisphereLight for atmosphere. Place 6 glowing checkpoint rings (using TorusGeometry with emissive MeshStandardMaterial, pulsating scale animation) at different street-level positions around the city. Interactions (8 steps with validation): (1) Press Enter to start the game and begin a 90-second countdown timer. (2) Use ArrowUp/ArrowDown to accelerate/brake the car with clamped speed between 0 and a max value. (3) Use ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to steer with smooth rotation. (4) Collide with checkpoint 1 (validate proximity < threshold) to collect it, triggering a particle burst effect and score increment. (5) Collect checkpoints 2 through 5 sequentially; each checkpoint only activates after the previous one is collected (validate order). (6) Press H to honk, which spawns a directional arrow UI pointing toward the next active checkpoint (validate that a checkpoint remains). (7) Collect the final checkpoint 6 to complete the rally. (8) Display a results panel showing total time, and a Restart button that resets car position, timer, and all checkpoints. Add a HUD overlay using HTML/CSS showing: current checkpoint number out of 6, elapsed time, and remaining time. Validate that the car cannot collect out-of-order checkpoints. Add a subtle engine hum sound effect using Web Audio API oscillator that changes pitch with speed. The city ground should have a contact shadow plane. Ensure the car has simple physics: velocity, friction deceleration, and collision boundary clamping so it stays within the city bounds.
